title: perf-benchmarking-sync-2026-04-28
content:
Perf Benchmarking Sync - 2026-04-28
Attendees: Aisha Patel (owner), Miguel Torres, Emily Chen, Daniel Kim, Rita Singh
Location: Zoom / #serving-runtime

Summary:
- We saw an unexpected regression in p95 latency and overall throughput on the nightly perf runs after merging the kernel selection change (PR #789). Regression shows up primarily for medium-length contexts (1k-2k tokens) on A100-80GB nodes.
- Baseline (2026-04-20 nightly): p50=34ms, p95=118ms, tokens/s=2,450 (batching: adaptive, kv-cache enabled)
- Current (2026-04-28 nightly): p50=38ms (+12%), p95=320ms (+171%), tokens/s=2,010 (-18%)
- Regression correlates with select-kernel fallback introduced in PR #789 (attention kernel heuristics). Suspect fallback triggers more often for variable sequence length batches, causing additional kernel warmups and reduced batching efficacy.

Repro steps / test runs performed:
- perfbench-v2 run: ./run_perfbench --model redwood-7B-qat --context 1024 --nodes a100-80gb --batching adaptive --kv-cache true --runs 30
  - Observed high variance across runs; outliers correspond to GPU kernel recompile/warmup windows.
- Isolated run without kv-cache: p95 drops to ~140ms, tokens/s ~2,240 -> kv-cache interactions are amplifying the regression.
- Run with fixed kernel selection (force-legacy-attn): p95 ~125ms, tokens/s ~2,410 -> confirms kernel selection change is major factor.
- Canary test on rtx-6000 series (non-prod): similar p95 increase but less severe (+60% vs +171%) -> behavior is hardware-dependent.

Investigation notes:
- PR #789 changed attention kernel heuristic to prefer new fused-attn kernel when avg-seq > 512; fallback path may not be caching kernel states across batches when context length varies.
- KV cache eviction/access patterns appear to cause different code paths (cache miss in middle of request) that trigger fallback and reinitialization.
- Scheduler metrics show increased queueing during 200-400ms windows when batches contain mixed short+long sequences.
- Driver/kernel logs show repeated cuLaunchKernel calls for the same op with slightly different launch configs (likely due to fallback).

Action items (owner, due):
- Miguel Torres: Add reproducible micro-benchmark that emulates mixed-length sequences and captures kernel selection traces (due 2026-05-01).
- Emily Chen: Add telemetry to perfbench to log kernel-choice, kernel-warmup events, and KV-cache hit/miss per request (due 2026-04-30).
- Daniel Kim: Revert the heuristic in a local branch and run week-long nightly tests to validate improvement (branch: revert/attn-heuristic, due 2026-05-03).
- Rita Singh: Measure impact on Dedicated autoscale policies and update SLO playbook if p95 remains >200ms for medium contexts (due 2026-05-05).
- Aisha Patel: Coordinate a cross-team triage meeting (eng-serving-runtime + infra + release-eng) to decide on a patch vs rollback by 2026-05-04.

Short-term mitigations tried:
- Forced legacy kernel selection for mixed batches in canary pool -> p95 improved to ~125ms.
- Temporarily disabled adaptive batching for 1k-2k context tests -> throughput dropped but p95 stabilised (useful as mitigation for critical customers).
- Increased KV-cache retention window -> modest improvement, not sufficient alone.

Notes for next sync:
- Miguel to present micro-benchmark results and kernel trace (2026-05-05 sync).
- Emily to share telemetry dashboard link and example logs (once implemented).
- Decision needed on whether to ship a targeted fix (avoid fallback churn) vs rolling back PR #789.

Misc:
- Affected customers: none reported production incidents yet; alerts only from nightly perf monitors and a CI canary.
- Priorities: fix to restore p95 for medium contexts before ramping new heuristic to wider fleet.

Attached quick links / commands for reproducing locally:
- perfbench command (example): 
  ./run_perfbench --model redwood-7B-qat --context 1536 --batching adaptive --kv-cache true --runs 50 --log-trace kernel_choice.log
- Kernel trace capture helper: scripts/trace_kernel_choice.sh

End of notes.
